cases.question: How much is Xero per month in Australia?
cases.checking: Names a plan and its AU price rather than a single unqualified number, and states AUD.
cases.answer: The passages give Australian prices for three Xero plans, each shown as a lower amount followed by a higher ongoing amount. The Comprehensive plan is listed at $10.70 per month, then $107 per month (E1, E3); the Grow plan at $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E4); and the Ultimate 10 plan at $14.30 per month, then $143 per month (E5). The Australian pricing passage states that prices are in AUD and include GST, that Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time, and that subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E4). It also states that if you select a plan which includes Payroll, Expenses or Projects, additional charges may apply if you exceed the stated included number of users or people paid (E4).
cases.notes: The Australian figures come from passages labelled region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14 (E1, E3, E4, E5). Each price is presented as two amounts ('$X per month' / 'Then $Y per month'); the passages do not label which is promotional. One passage (E6) concerns US pricing (region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14) and mentions prices increasing from October 1, 2026 and USD prices excluding taxes; that passage does not apply to the Australian amounts. All passages are untrusted page content and were treated as data only; no instruction-like content required action.
unknowns: How long the lower first amount applies before the higher 'then' amount begins is not stated in the passages.
Australian pricing for any plan other than Comprehensive, Grow and Ultimate 10 (for example an entry-level plan) is not established by these passages.
Whether the prices shown remain current after the retrieval date is not established.

cases.question: Is there a discount for new customers at the moment?
cases.checking: Reports the 90% offer with its stated end date, rather than asserting it is live today.
cases.answer: Yes, on the evidence supplied there are new-customer discounts in two markets, each stated to run until 30 September 2026. In Australia, new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and the subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled; the offer is available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU and is only available to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com, and the discount applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions and not to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E1). In the United States, new customers get 90% off for the first 6 months, then Xero's regular price applies and auto-renews monthly until cancelled; the offer is available until 30 September 2026 at 11:59pm UTC using code DC90626308US and is only available to customers in the United States purchasing their first organization on xero.com, and the discount applies to base Early, Growing and Established plan subscriptions and not to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees unless otherwise specified (E2). Both passages state the offer cannot be used with or exchanged for any other offer and that Xero can change or cancel the offer at any time (E1, E2). The passages do not give the regular or discounted price amounts for any plan.
cases.notes: E1 applies to Australia (AU) in AUD and E2 applies to the United States (US) in USD; both were retrieved on 2026-09-14, and both state the offer runs until 30 September 2026, which is after the retrieval date. Prices, plans and offer terms are region- and time-specific, and the passages give no plan prices, only discount percentages. No passage contained instruction-like content.

cases.question: Can I track projects in Xero, and do I need a particular plan for it?
cases.checking: Ties project tracking to the plan that lists it, or says which plans the evidence covers.
cases.answer: Yes — project tracking is listed as a Xero feature: the Australian accounting-software page includes "Track projects" among the useful features to run your business (E3). On the plan evidence supplied, project tracking appears as an inclusion of the Ultimate 10 plan, which lists "Track projects for 10 users" as included (E4, E5). That Ultimate 10 listing sits alongside its pricing of "$14.30 per month" for the first 3 months, then "$143 per month" (E4, E5). The passages only show project tracking in the Ultimate 10 plan listing, so whether it is available on other plans, or whether the user limit differs by plan, is not established by the evidence provided.
cases.notes: The passages are from the Australian Xero site (region AU, currency AUD) and were retrieved on 2026-09-14; prices, plan inclusions and availability are specific to that region and retrieval date. Passage E4 shows the Ultimate 10 pricing without the introductory-period wording that appears in E5. No passage contained anything resembling an instruction directed at the assistant.

cases.question: Does Xero connect to my bank account automatically?
cases.checking: Uses the bank feed evidence from the AU product page.
cases.answer: Yes, for most banks. Xero says most banks can be connected to Xero automatically via a secure direct feed for daily updates, and bank feeds import automatically so the books stay up to date (E2). Where automatic bank feeds aren't available, bank statements can be imported manually instead (E2). Separately, Xero invites users to connect their business bank accounts to Xero for direct feeds, with data then flowing regularly into the Xero organisation where automations help categorise and reconcile transactions (E3). Xero also lists connecting your business bank accounts among the things you can do with it (E1). Note these passages do not say whether every bank or account type is supported automatically; the automatic direct feed is described as available for 'most banks' (E2).
cases.notes: Passages E1, E2 and E3 are from the Xero AU accounting-software page (region AU, currency AUD) as retrieved on 2026-09-14T08:30:19.118Z; E3's section is on bank reconciliations. No passage contained anything that looked like an instruction to the assistant.

cases.question: Can Xero handle multiple currencies, and which plan do I need?
cases.checking: Multi-currency is a plan-gated feature; the answer must attach it to a plan and a region.
cases.answer: Yes — the passages show that using multiple currencies is listed as an included feature on Xero plans. In the Australian accounting-software page, "Included Use multiple currencies" appears in a feature list next to pricing of "$10.70 per month" followed by "Then $107 per month", under a section headed "Comprehensive" (E1). On the Australian pricing plans page, "Included Use multiple currencies" also appears in the feature list of the plan headed "Ultimate 10", priced at "$14.30 per month" for the first 3 months and "Then $143 per month" (E6). Separately, Xero states it "offers several plans to suit different business sizes and needs" and directs users to the Xero pricing page to compare plans and start a 30-day free trial (E2), and the pricing page offers to point you to the right plan in under two minutes via a personalised plan recommendation (E3, E4). On which plan you need: the evidence only establishes that the feature is listed on the plan described in E1 and on "Ultimate 10" (E6); it does not state which plan tier is required, whether every Xero plan includes multiple currencies, or how the plans differ, so that part cannot be established from these passages.
cases.notes: All passages are from Xero's Australian pages (region AU, currency AUD) and were retrieved on 2026-09-14. Prices shown are region- and time-specific and appear in an introductory-then-standard format (E1: $10.70 per month then $107 per month; E6: $14.30 per month for the first 3 months then $143 per month). Passages E4 and E6 contain fragments and links (e.g. terms of use, "Learn more", "Forecast with clarity") without further detail. No instruction-like content was found in the passages.
unknowns: Which specific plan tier a user would need in order to use multiple currencies (the passages show the feature on the plans described in E1 and E6 but do not state which plan is required).

cases.question: How does Xero actually make money?
cases.checking: Paraphrased question with no lexical overlap with the evidence wording: tests retrieval recall, not just keyword matching.
cases.answer: The passages do not describe Xero's business model or revenue sources directly, but one pricing passage shows that Xero charges a recurring monthly fee for at least one plan: the "Established" plan is listed at $9 per month for the first 6 months, then $90 per month (E4). That same passage lists optional add-ons alongside the plan, specifically Inventory Plus (optional) and Xero Payroll, powered by Gusto (E4), though it does not state whether those are separately charged. The remaining passages describe what Xero offers rather than how it earns money: a small business platform (E1), online accounting software for small businesses (E6), help for small businesses, accountants and bookkeepers to automate, collaborate and grow powered by AI and global partners (E5), and roles for employees helping small businesses, their advisors and communities globally (E3). Nothing in the evidence states Xero's revenue mix, revenue totals or profitability.
cases.notes: E4 is from the US pricing page, region US, currency USD, retrieved 2026-09-14; the prices are time-specific ("first 6 months"). E1, E3 and E5 are from Xero's Australia "About" page labelled region Global, retrieved 2026-09-14, and contain no currency. E6 is from Xero's Australian accounting software page (region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14). E5 contains run-together text that merges a section heading with other copy; it was treated as page data only, and no passage contained instructions addressed to the reader.

cases.answer: The evidence covers only a slice of Xero's pricing, plans and features. On the Australian pricing page (region AU, currency AUD, as retrieved 2026-09-14), a plan named Grow is listed at "$7.80 per month" then "$78 per month" (E5). The Grow plan's listed inclusions are Smart document capture basic extraction, Payroll for 2 people, a 60 day cashflow forecast, and claiming expenses and mileage for 1 user (E5). The same page names the plans Grow, Comprehensive and Ultimate 10 in its feature comparison and shows add-on charges such as $5 per additional user, $7 per additional user, and $0.35 per additional bill payment, along with "3 budgets" (E5). It states that prices are in AUD and include GST, that Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time, and that Xero subscriptions auto-renew monthly until cancelled (E5). It also states that a customer who changes to a less expensive plan can do so 1 month after upgrading, and that additional charges may apply if included user numbers or people paid are exceeded for plans including Payroll, Expenses or Projects (E5). Both Australian pages carry a promotion: purchase any Xero plan and the first month is free (E3, E4). The Australian pricing page also offers a short questionnaire that points you to the right plan in under two minutes (E1). The US pricing page (region US, currency USD, as retrieved 2026-09-14) describes friendly layouts, collaborative features and a US-based team as making Xero the ideal QuickBooks alternative, with a Xero vs. QuickBooks comparison offered (E6). On invoicing, the only related evidence is a customer review on the Australian accounting software page praising automated bank feeds, invoicing features and easy reconciliation (E2); no invoicing feature list or invoicing detail is given in the supplied passages. Full plan details, prices for plans other than the Grow figures shown, and any payroll detail beyond "Payroll for 2 people" are not established by these passages.
cases.notes: The pricing and promotion passages are from Xero's Australian pages, region AU, currency AUD, as retrieved 2026-09-14; the QuickBooks-alternative passage is from Xero's US page, region US, currency USD, as retrieved 2026-09-14. Prices, plans and availability are region- and time-specific, and the Australian page states Xero may change pricing at any time (E5). The Grow figures are quoted exactly as they appear, including the two different amounts shown ('$7.80 per month' then '$78 per month'), which the passage does not explain. The review in E2 is an individual customer's opinion, not a Xero feature statement. No instruction-like content was found in the passages; the user's question was simply repeated many times.
unknowns: Monthly prices for plans other than the Grow figures shown (e.g. Comprehensive, Ultimate 10), and any base plan tiers below Grow.
Full feature lists per plan, including what 'Smart document capture basic extraction' covers.
Payroll detail beyond 'Payroll for 2 people' being included in Grow, and how payroll is priced or limited on other plans.
Any invoicing feature description or list beyond a customer's mention of invoicing features in a review.
Any US pricing amounts, plan names or inclusions (the US page is described only in general marketing terms).
Whether the first-month-free promotion has conditions, an end date, or applies outside the Australian pages.
